_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES USED: idx 2, 4, 6 ONLY. Full page map, all 8 accounted for: idx0 = cover (bilingual, SET-2, Q.P. Code 65/1/2, 'Page 1 of 8'); idx1 = HINDI General Instructions + Section A Q1-6; idx2 = ENGLISH General Instructions + SECTION-A Q1-6; idx3 = HINDI Section B Q7-10 + Section C header + Q11; idx4 = ENGLISH SECTION-B Q7-10 + SECTION-C header + Q11; idx5 = HINDI Q12-14; idx6 = ENGLISH Q12-14; idx7 = 'Page 8 of 8', BLANK apart from a QR code, an asterisk and the footer. The booklet is chunked Hindi-block-then-English-block, NOT page-alternating end-to-end, so English is idx 2/4/6 and there are only three English pages. NO overflow of one language onto the other's page: every Hindi page ends on a completed question (idx1 at Q6, idx3 at Q11, idx5 at Q14(ii)) and so does every English page, so no English text sits at the top of any odd index and the last page carries none either. Each odd page was opened at full size and checked rather than assumed; idx3's Hindi mirrors the English Section B question-for-question (same OR placement at Q8 and Q9), which independently corroborates that the English Section B is complete. STRUCTURE (printed General Instructions, idx2): three Sections; A = Q1-6 short answer type-I @2, B = Q7-10 short answer type-II @3, C = Q11-14 long answer @4, with (vii) Q14 a case based problem with 2 subparts of 2 marks each. Marks sum 12+12+16 = 40, matching the marking scheme's 'Maximum Marks: 40'. NO MCQs anywhere - every question is subjective, so no options, no answer letters, and no key re-derivation applies. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (vi) reads only 'There is an internal choice in some questions' and prints NO counts, so the count was established by reading the paper and then confirmed question-by-question against the official marking scheme (ms/p02-p10, paper code 65/1/2), which reprints both branches. FOUR internal choices: Q1, Q8, Q9, Q13 - each printed (a) / OR / (b). Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q14 carry no alternative. 19 rows = 14 questions + 4 OR-alternatives + 1 extra case-study sub-part. OVERLAP WITH 65/1/1: 14 of the 19 rows are the same question, judged by CONTENT against data/2022-65-1-1.questions.json, confirmed on this paper's own pages, then reused byte-for-byte so they dedup at commit. The sets are RESHUFFLED and renumbered: this paper's Q1 = 65/1/1 Q3, Q2 = Q4, Q3 = Q5, Q4 = Q6, Q6 = Q2, Q7 = Q10, Q8 = Q7, Q11 = Q13, Q13 = Q11, Q14 = Q14. FIVE rows are genuinely new: Q5 (solve log(dy/dx) = x - y), Q9a (integral of (x^3+x)/(x^4-9)), Q9b (definite integral of (3 sin x - 2)^2 over -pi to pi), Q10 (point on a line at distance 5 from a point) and Q12 (Bayes, doublet). 65/1/1's Q1 (order + degree) and its Q9 (both branches) do not appear in this set at all. plan.txt WAS MISLEADING and was not relied on: it claimed 0 already-covered and 13 new, against an actual overlap of 10 of its 13 marking-scheme blocks, and of its 5 perceptual hints 4 were right and 1 was FALSE - 'Q5 ~ 65/1/1 Q1' is wrong (both are 2-mark differential equations, but this paper's Q5 is a fresh variables-separable question), while it missed Q2, Q3, Q4, Q6, Q7 and Q8, every one of which IS a duplicate. Judged by content throughout. SYLLABUS NOTE: this is the COVID-era Term-2 paper set on the PRE-rationalisation syllabus. Q4 examines the distance of a point from a PLANE and is filed on the 'The Plane' subtopic added 2026-08-19 for exactly this case. Unlike 65/1/1 this set has only ONE plane question - 65/1/1's Q8 (plane through the intersection of two planes) is absent here. MARKING-SCHEME DEFECT, noted for the answer-authoring step and NOT affecting any stem: the Sol. to Q6 (ms/p04) prints 'PR = PQ + PS therefore PS = PR', which is nonsense as written; every subsequent line and both printed answers (|PR| = 2 sqrt 2, |QS| = 6) are correct, so it is a typeset slip in the scheme, not a wrong method.

questions.stem: If \(\frac{d}{dx}[F(x)] = \frac{\sec^4 x}{\operatorname{cosec}^4 x}\) and \(F\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\pi}{4}\), then find \(F(x)\).
Let A and B be two events such that \(P(A) = \frac{5}{8}\), \(P(B) = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(P(A/B) = \frac{3}{4}\). Find the value of \(P(B/A)\).
Two balls are drawn at random from a bag containing 2 red balls and 3 blue balls, without replacement. Let the variable X denotes the number of red balls. Find the probability distribution of X.
questions._flag: Printed as 'Let the variable X denotes the number of red balls' - the printed subject-verb agreement is wrong ('denotes' for 'denote'). Transcribed as printed; the question is unambiguous. Same defect is printed in 65/1/1 Q5, so it is the shared typeset block, not a per-set slip.

questions.stem: Find the values of \(\lambda\), for which the distance of point \((2, 1, \lambda)\) from plane \(3x + 5y + 4z = 11\) is \(2\sqrt{2}\) units.
Solve the differential equation : \(\log\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = x - y\).
In a parallelogram PQRS, \(\overrightarrow{PQ} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\) and \(\overrightarrow{PS} = -\hat{i} - 2\hat{k}\). Find \(|\overrightarrow{PR}|\) and \(|\overrightarrow{QS}|\).
Find the particular solution of the differential equation \(x\frac{dy}{dx} + x\cos^2\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) = y\); given that when \(x = 1\), \(y = \frac{\pi}{4}\).

If \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\), \(\vec{c}\) and \(\vec{d}\) are four non-zero vectors such that \(\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{c} \times \vec{d}\) and \(\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = 4\vec{b} \times \vec{d}\), then show that \((\vec{a} - 2\vec{d})\) is parallel to \((2\vec{b} - \vec{c})\) where \(\vec{a} \neq 2\vec{d}\), \(\vec{c} \neq 2\vec{b}\).

The two adjacent sides of a parallelogram are represented by \(2\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}\) and \(2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\). Find the unit vectors parallel to its diagonals. Using the diagonal vectors, find the area of the parallelogram also.

questions.subtopic: Equation of a Line in Space
questions.stem: Find the co-ordinates of the point on the line \(\frac{x + 2}{3} = \frac{y + 1}{2} = \frac{z - 3}{2}\) which is at a distance of 5 units from the point \((1, 3, 3)\).
A man is known to speak truth 7 out of 10 times. He threw a pair of dice and reports that doublet appeared. Find the probability that it was actually a doublet.

questions.subtopic: Area Bounded by a Curve and a Line
questions.stem: Using integration, find the area of the region \(\{(x, y) : 4x^2 + 9y^2 \leq 36, 2x + 3y \geq 6\}\).
Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by lines \(x - y + 1 = 0\), \(x = -2\), \(x = 3\) and \(x\)-axis.

questions.context:
Electrical transmission wires which are laid down in winters are stretched tightly to accommodate expansion in summers.
Two such wires lie along the following lines :
\(l_1 : \frac{x + 1}{3} = \frac{y - 3}{-2} = \frac{z + 2}{-1}\)
\(l_2 : \frac{x}{-1} = \frac{y - 7}{3} = \frac{z + 7}{-2}\)
Based on the given information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Are the lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) coplanar ? Justify your answer.
questions._figure: DECORATIVE - a captioned photograph of an electrical transmission tower (labels: Grounded metal tower, Overhead ground wires, Nearest three phase conductors, Insulators). It carries no data; both line equations are printed in the text. Page idx 6.
